questions.question: In 2025, how much permanent monthly alimony did the Supreme Court set for a divorced but unmarried wife?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹50,000**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a landmark ruling in **2025**, the **Supreme Court of India** reinforced the financial security of women by setting a permanent monthly alimony benchmark of **₹50,000** for a divorced wife who remains unmarried.
 
• The **Apex Court** emphasized that maintenance is not a matter of charity but a fundamental right derived from the principle of **Social Justice**, ensuring that a woman is not left in a state of destitution after the dissolution of marriage.
 
• The judgment clarified that the amount of **₹50,000** was determined considering the rising **Cost of Living** and the **Inflation Index**, aiming to provide a basic standard of living that aligns with the husband's financial status and the wife's previous lifestyle.
 
• This decision is rooted in the interpretation of **Section 125** of the **Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC)**, now integrated into the **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS)**, which mandates the husband to provide support to a wife who is unable to maintain herself.
 
• The court highlighted that the 'unmarried' status of the divorced wife necessitates continuous support until her remarriage or change in financial circumstances, making the **₹50,000** sum a fixed monthly obligation for the respondent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Permanent Alimony**:

 
 
• It refers to the allowance ordered by the court to be paid by one spouse to the other after the **Decree of Divorce** is passed.
 
• Under **Section 25** of the **Hindu Marriage Act, 1955**, the court has the authority to grant permanent alimony and maintenance at the time of passing any decree.
 
 
 
• **Factors Influencing Alimony Quantum**:
 
 
• **Standard of Living**: The **Supreme Court** has consistently held that a wife is entitled to the same comfort level she enjoyed in her **Matrimonial Home**.
 
• **Financial Capacity**: The **Net Taxable Income**, assets, and liabilities of the husband are critical determinants for the final amount.
 
• **Duration of Marriage**: Longer durations often lead to higher alimony settlements due to the increased dependency established over time.
 
 
 
• **Interim Maintenance**:
 
 
• Distinguished from permanent alimony, this is the amount paid during the pendency of the **Matrimonial Suit** to cover immediate legal and living expenses.

questions.question: Who among the following administers oath of Pro Tem Speaker during initial sitting of newly elected Lok Sabha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Speaker Pro Tem** is a temporary post created to preside over the first few sittings of a newly elected **Lok Sabha** until a permanent **Speaker** is elected.
 
• According to **Article 99** of the **Indian Constitution**, every member of either House of Parliament must, before taking their seat, make and subscribe an oath or affirmation before the **President** or some person appointed by him.
 
• The **President of India** appoints the **Speaker Pro Tem** and administers the oath of office to him/her, usually at the **Rashtrapati Bhavan**, before the first session of the new House begins.
 
• By convention, the most senior member of the **Lok Sabha** (in terms of number of years/terms served) is chosen for this position to ensure the smooth transition of parliamentary proceedings.
 
• The primary duties of the **Speaker Pro Tem** include presiding over the first meeting of the **Lok Sabha**, administering the oath to all other newly elected members, and enabling the election of the permanent **Speaker**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chief Justice of India**:

 
 
• Responsible for administering the oath of office to the **President of India** under **Article 60**.
 
• Does not have a constitutional role in the administration of oaths for members of the **Legislature**.
 
 
 
• **Vice President of India**:
 
 
• Acts as the **Ex-officio Chairman** of the **Rajya Sabha**.
 
• The oath of the **Vice President** is administered by the **President** or a person appointed by him.
 
 
 
• **Cabinet Secretary**:
 
 
• The highest-ranking civil servant and the administrative head of the **Cabinet Secretariat**.
 
• Functions as the chief coordinator of the **Government of India** but holds no constitutional authority regarding parliamentary oaths.
 
 
 
• **Nature of Office**:
 
 
• The office of **Speaker Pro Tem** is strictly temporary and ceases to exist the moment the House elects its permanent **Speaker** under **Article 93**.

questions.question: Which of the following sequences correctly matches the coastal sections from north to south on the western coast?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Konkan → Karnataka → Malabar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Western Coastal Plain** of India is a narrow strip of land situated between the **Western Ghats** and the **Arabian Sea**, extending from the **Gulf of Kachchh** in the north to **Kanyakumari** in the south.
 
• The **Konkan Coast** constitutes the northern segment of the western coastline. It stretches from **Daman** in the north to **Goa** in the south, covering the coastal districts of **Maharashtra** and **Goa**. It is characterized by a rugged and indented coastline.
 
• The **Karnataka Coast**, also referred to as the **Kanara Coast**, is the middle section located south of the Konkan region. It extends from **Goa** to **Mangalore** along the state of **Karnataka**.
 
• The **Malabar Coast** forms the southernmost part of the western coastal plains, stretching from **Mangalore** to the southern tip of the peninsula at **Kanyakumari**. This region primarily falls within the state of **Kerala** and is known for its extensive **backwaters** or **Kayals**.
 
• Therefore, the correct geographical sequence from north to south along the western coast is the **Konkan Coast**, followed by the **Karnataka Coast**, and finally the **Malabar Coast**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathiawar Coast**:

 
 
• This section is located in **Gujarat**, specifically around the **Saurashtra** peninsula. It lies to the north of the **Konkan Coast** and is bounded by the **Gulf of Kachchh** and the **Gulf of Khambhat**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with the Eastern Coast**:
 
 
• The **Eastern Coastal Plain** is broader than the western coast and is divided into the **Northern Circars** (between the Mahanadi and Krishna rivers) and the **Coromandel Coast** (stretching from the Krishna river to Kanyakumari).
 
 
 
• **Geomorphological Features**:
 
 
• The western coast is an example of a **submerged coast**, which provides natural deep-water harbors. Major ports such as **Kandla**, **Mumbai**, **Marmagao**, and **Kochi** are located along this coastline.

questions.question: Programs like MS Word, MS Excel, and PowerPoint fall into which group?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Application software**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Application software** consists of programs designed to perform specific tasks for users, rather than simply managing the computer system itself.
 
• **Microsoft Word** is categorized as a **word processor** used for creating, editing, and formatting text documents.
 
• **Microsoft Excel** is a **spreadsheet application** utilized for data organization, mathematical calculations, and financial analysis using a grid of cells.
 
• **Microsoft PowerPoint** is a **presentation program** that allows users to create visual slide decks for business or educational purposes.
 
• These programs are considered **end-user software** because they allow individuals to produce specific outputs like documents, charts, and presentations.
 
• Application software requires an **Operating System** to run, as it does not communicate directly with the computer **hardware**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **System software**:

 
 
• Responsible for managing and controlling the **hardware components** so that application software can perform its tasks.
 
• Core examples include **Operating Systems (OS)** like **Windows 11**, **Linux**, and **macOS**, as well as **utility software** like disk defragmenters.
 
 
 
• **Hardware components**:
 
 
• The physical, tangible parts of a computer system such as the **Central Processing Unit (CPU)**, **Hard Disk Drive (HDD)**, and **Monitor**.
 
 
 
• **Booting programs**:
 
 
• Specific sets of instructions, such as the **BIOS (Basic Input/Output System)** or **UEFI**, that load the operating system into the **RAM** when the computer is turned on.

questions.question: Microlithic tools became a characteristic feature during which phase of prehistory in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mesolithic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mesolithic** phase, also referred to as the **Middle Stone Age**, represents a transitional period between the **Palaeolithic** and **Neolithic** eras, beginning approximately around **10,000 BCE** in India.
 
• The most defining technological advancement of this period was the production of **microliths**, which are tiny, highly specialized stone tools made from crypto-crystalline silica such as **chert**, **chalcedony**, **agate**, and **jasper**.
 
• These tools are typically very small, ranging from **1 cm to 8 cm** in length, and are classified into **geometrical** shapes (like **triangles**, **trapezes**, and **lunates** or crescents) and **non-geometrical** shapes.
 
• **Microliths** were rarely used alone; they were designed to be **hafted** into wooden or bone handles to create composite tools like **spearheads**, **arrowheads**, **knives**, and **sickles**.
 
• In the Indian context, major **Mesolithic** sites include **Bagor** in Rajasthan (one of the largest Mesolithic sites), **Adamgarh** in Madhya Pradesh, **Langhnaj** in Gujarat, and **Sarai Nahar Rai** in Uttar Pradesh.
 
• This era witnessed a shift towards more efficient hunting-gathering and the early beginnings of **animal domestication**, as evidenced by findings at **Bagor** and **Adamgarh**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lower Palaeolithic**

 
 
• Characterized by the **Acheulian** culture involving large, heavy stone tools.
 
• Common implements included **hand-axes**, **cleavers**, and **choppers** used for butchering and digging.
 
 
 
• **Middle Palaeolithic**
 
 
• Marked by a transition to **flake-based** tool industries.
 
• Key tools included **scrapers**, **borers**, and **points** made using the **Levallois technique**.
 
 
 
• **Early Iron Age**
 
 
• Associated with the introduction of **iron metallurgy** following the **Bronze Age**.
 
• In India, this period is often linked with the **Painted Grey Ware (PGW)** culture in the North and **Megalithic** cultures in the South.

questions.question: Which pact between Gandhi and the British government marked the suspension of the Civil Disobedience Movement in 1931?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gandhi-Irwin Pact**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Gandhi-Irwin Pact** was a landmark political agreement signed on **March 5, 1931**, between **Mahatma Gandhi** and the **Viceroy of India**, **Lord Irwin**, before the **Second Round Table Conference** in **London**.
 
• The pact led to the **suspension** of the **Civil Disobedience Movement**, which had gained massive momentum following the **Salt Satyagraha** and the **Dandi March** of **1930**.
 
• Key provisions of the pact included the **release** of all **political prisoners** not charged with violence, the **return** of confiscated properties to their owners, and the right of people in coastal villages to **make salt** for personal consumption without paying tax.
 
• In exchange, the **Indian National Congress** agreed to discontinue the movement and participate in the **Second Round Table Conference** to discuss constitutional reforms for **India**.
 
• The pact was significant as it placed the **Indian National Congress** on an equal footing with the **British Government** for the first time during negotiations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Poona Pact (1932)**:

 
 
• This was an agreement between **Mahatma Gandhi** and **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar** on behalf of the **depressed classes** and upper-caste Hindus.
 
• It resulted in the **reservation** of seats for the **Depressed Classes** in provincial and central legislatures instead of **separate electorates**.
 
 
 
• **Lucknow Pact (1916)**:
 
 
• An agreement reached between the **Indian National Congress** and the **All India Muslim League** at a joint session held in **Lucknow**.
 
• It established a **joint front** to demand **self-government** from the British and accepted the principle of **separate electorates** for Muslims.
 
 
 
• **Lahore Session (1929)**:
 
 
• Presided over by **Jawaharlal Nehru**, this session is famous for passing the resolution of **Purna Swaraj** or **Complete Independence**, which set the stage for the **Civil Disobedience Movement**.

questions.question: Why was the Partition of Bengal (1905) widely opposed by Indian nationalists?

options.text: It was planned to improve agricultural administration and address recurring famine conditions.
It was intended to divide people on communal lines and weaken the growing nationalist movement.
It was undertaken to promote regional trade expansion and economic integration of eastern Bengal.
It was proposed to relocate the colonial capital for better administrative coordination.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It was intended to divide people on communal lines and weaken the growing nationalist movement.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Partition of Bengal** was announced on **July 19, 1905**, by the then Viceroy of India, **Lord Curzon**, and it officially came into effect on **October 16, 1905**.
 
• While the British administration cited **administrative convenience** as the official reason, the actual strategic intent was to stifle the rising tide of **Indian nationalism**, as **Bengal** was the nerve center of political consciousness and anti-colonial resistance.
 
• The territorial reorganization was designed to create a communal rift by establishing a **Muslim-majority** province in the East (**Eastern Bengal and Assam**) and a **Hindu-majority** province in the West (**Western Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha**).
 
• By making the Bengali-speaking population a minority in their own province and fostering religious divisions, the colonial government aimed to implement the classic **Divide and Rule** policy to weaken the unified front of the **Indian National Congress**.
 
• Nationalist leaders recognized this as a deliberate attempt to destroy **Bengali unity** and communal harmony, leading to the launch of the **Swadeshi** and **Boycott** movements, which marked a new phase in the struggle for **Swaraj**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Swadeshi Movement**:

 
 
• It was a direct reaction to the **1905 Partition**, emphasizing the use of indigenous goods and the burning of foreign-made cloth to exert economic pressure on the British.
 
 
 
• **1911 Annulment**:
 
 
• Due to the intense and sustained political agitation, the partition was eventually annulled by **Lord Hardinge** during the **Delhi Durbar** in **1911**.
 
 
 
• **Administrative Rationale**:
 
 
• The British argued that the **Bengal Presidency** was too large, with a population of nearly **78 million**, making it difficult for a single Lieutenant-Governor to manage effectively.
 
 
 
• **Shift of Capital**:
 
 
• In **1911**, alongside the annulment of the partition, the British shifted the capital of colonial India from **Calcutta** to **Delhi** to ensure better administrative control and move away from the revolutionary hotbed of Bengal.

questions.question: Where is the headquarters of the South Western Railway Zone located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hubballi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **South Western Railway (SWR)** is one of the **19 railway zones** in India, which was created by reorganizing the existing **Southern Railway** and **South Central Railway** zones.
 
• The zone officially commenced its operations on **April 1, 2003**, with its headquarters established in **Hubballi** (formerly known as **Hubli**) in the state of **Karnataka**.
 
• Geographically, the **South Western Railway** zone covers a vast majority of the railway network in **Karnataka**, and extends its jurisdiction to parts of **Tamil Nadu**, **Andhra Pradesh**, and **Goa**.
 
• The administrative structure of this zone is divided into three functional divisions: **Hubballi**, **Bengaluru**, and **Mysuru**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly explains the decline of metallic coins in the post-Gupta period?

options.text: It happened because rulers preferred using older coins rather than minting new ones.
It occurred due to abundant commerce that reduced dependence on minted currency.
It emerged because gold supplies increased and made minting coins unnecessary.
It resulted from reduced trade and rising land grants replacing cash payments.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It resulted from reduced trade and rising land grants replacing cash payments.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **post-Gupta period** (6th century CE to 1000 CE) was characterized by a distinct shift from a centralized monetary economy to a decentralized **agrarian structure**.
 
• A primary cause for the decline in **metallic coinage** was the **slump in long-distance trade**, particularly with the **Roman Empire** and **Central Asia**, which reduced the influx of gold and silver.
 
• Economic historians like **R.S. Sharma** argue that the emergence of **Indian Feudalism** led to the practice of **land grants**. Rulers began donating land to **Brahmins (Agraharas)** and state officials as a substitute for **cash salaries**.
 
• This transition promoted a **closed, self-sufficient village economy** where local production met local needs, significantly diminishing the necessity for a circulating **metallic currency** for daily transactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Currency Alternatives**:

 
 
• While high-value gold and silver coins became scarce, **cowrie shells** (shells used as money) and **copper coins** became the standard medium for small-scale **local exchange**.
 
 
 
• **Gupta Coinage**:
 
 
• The **Gupta Dynasty** was famous for its high-quality **gold coins (Dinaras)**; however, toward the end of their rule, coins showed increasing **debasement** (mixing gold with inferior metals), signaling economic distress.
 
 
 
• **Urban Decay**:
 
 
• The decline of trade led to **urban centers** falling into ruin, forcing merchants and artisans to move to rural areas, which further solidified **land-based wealth** over **monetary wealth**.

questions.question: In which year the 89th Constitutional Amendment was passed related to the National Commission for Scheduled Castes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2003**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **89th Constitutional Amendment Act** was enacted in the year **2003** to bifurcate the combined National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
 
• This amendment specifically aimed at creating a dedicated **National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC)** under **Article 338** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The act also inserted a new **Article 338A**, which led to the establishment of the **National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST)**.
 
• This legislative change was passed by the Parliament in **2003** and received the **Presidential assent** shortly thereafter, officially coming into force on **February 19, 2004**.
 
• Before this amendment, the **65th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1990** had replaced the one-man Special Officer with a multi-member **National Commission for SCs and STs**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC)**:

 
 
• It is a **constitutional body** responsible for safeguarding the interests of the Scheduled Castes in India.
 
• The commission consists of a **Chairperson**, a **Vice-Chairperson**, and **three other members**, all of whom are appointed by the **President of India** by warrant under his hand and seal.
 
• Their primary function is to investigate and monitor all matters relating to the safeguards provided for the **Scheduled Castes** under the Constitution or any other law.
 
• The commission has all the powers of a **civil court** while investigating any matter or inquiring into any complaint.
 
 
 
• **Reasons for Bifurcation**:
 
 
• The social and educational conditions of **Scheduled Tribes** were considered significantly different from **Scheduled Castes**, as STs often face issues related to geographical isolation and cultural preservation, whereas SCs face issues related to social exclusion like **untouchability**.
 
• Separating the commissions allowed for a more focused approach toward the specific development and **welfare schemes** tailored for each group.

questions.question:
Identify the classical language(s) in India (as of December 2022) from among the following.

1) Marathi

2) Tamil

3) Sanskrit

4) Odia
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 2, 3 and 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Marathi**: As of **December 2022**, this language did not hold the official classical status. Although the **Maharashtra Government** submitted a proposal based on the **Rangnath Pathare Committee** report, the **Union Cabinet** only granted it **Classical Language** status later in **October 2024**. Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.
 
• **Tamil**: It was the very first language in **India** to be accorded the **Classical Language** status in **2004**. The criteria for this selection include high antiquity of early texts and a recorded history spanning over **1500 to 2000 years**. Hence, statement 2 is correct.
 
• **Sanskrit**: This language was declared classical in **2005**. It is recognized for its extraordinary contribution to **Indian** heritage, particularly through the **Vedas**, **Upanishads**, and classical literature that influenced several other linguistic traditions. Hence, statement 3 is correct.
 
• **Odia**: It was officially added to the list in **February 2014**, becoming the sixth language to receive this distinction. It was the first language from the **Indo-Aryan** group, other than Sanskrit, to be recognized as classical during that period. Hence, statement 4 is correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• As of **December 2022**, there were a total of **six** languages recognized as classical by the **Ministry of Culture**:

 
 
• **Tamil** (declared in **2004**).
 
• **Sanskrit** (declared in **2005**).
 
• **Kannada** (declared in **2008**).
 
• **Telugu** (declared in **2008**).
 
• **Malayalam** (declared in **2013**).
 
• **Odia** (declared in **2014**).
 
 
 
• The **Linguistic Experts Committee**, constituted by the **Ministry of Culture**, evaluates the eligibility of languages based on original literary traditions that are not borrowed from another speech community.
 
• Benefits of this status include the establishment of a **Center of Excellence for Studies in Classical Languages** and the provision for the **University Grants Commission** (UGC) to create professional chairs in **Central Universities** for these specific languages.

questions.question: Where was the 353rd International Labor Organization Governing body meeting held in March 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Geneva, Switzerland**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **353rd Session** of the **Governing Body** of the **International Labour Organization (ILO)** is scheduled to be held in **March 2025**.
 
• This session, like most regular meetings of the executive council, takes place at the **ILO Headquarters** in **Geneva, Switzerland**.
 
• The **Governing Body** is the executive organ of the **ILO** and meets three times a year, specifically in **March**, **June**, and **October/November**, to make decisions on **ILO policy**, the agenda of the **International Labour Conference**, and the draft **Programme and Budget**.
 
• During these sessions, representatives discuss global labor standards, the protection of workers rights, and the implementation of international labor conventions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **International Labour Organization (ILO)**:

 
 
• It was founded in **1919** under the **Treaty of Versailles** as an affiliated agency of the **League of Nations**.
 
• In **1946**, it became the first specialized agency associated with the **United Nations (UN)**.
 
• The organization is unique due to its **tripartite structure**, which involves **governments**, **employers**, and **workers** from **187 Member States** in its decision-making processes.
 
• The **ILO** was awarded the **Nobel Peace Prize** in **1969** for its work in improving fraternity and peace among nations through social justice.
 
• The current **Director-General** of the **ILO** (as of 2024-2025) is **Gilbert F. Houngbo**, who was elected by the **Governing Body**.

questions.question: Which Indian state secured the highest number of gold medals at the Khelo India Water Sports Festival, 2025?

__

questions.question: Which unique architectural feature distinguishes the Harappan site of Dholavira?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Step-wells for water conservation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dholavira**, located on **Khadir Bet** island in the **Kutch Desert Wildlife Sanctuary** of **Gujarat**, is distinguished by its extraordinary **water management system**.
 
• Archaeologists discovered a massive, **rectangular step-well** at the site, measuring approximately **73.4 meters** in length, **29.3 meters** in width, and **10 meters** in depth.
 
• This prehistoric **step-well** is nearly three times the size of the **Great Bath** at **Mohenjo-daro** and represents one of the earliest and most sophisticated examples of **hydraulic engineering** in the ancient world.
 
• The site features a series of **16 interconnected reservoirs** and stone-cut **dams** designed to conserve every drop of rainwater in an otherwise **arid environment**.
 
• The presence of these **rock-cut** water structures highlights the transition from simple **well-culture** to advanced **water harvesting**, making it a unique architectural hallmark of this specific **Harappan** city.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **City Planning and Structure**:

 
 
• Unlike most **Harappan** cities which were divided into two parts (the **Citadel** and the **Lower Town**), **Dholavira** was uniquely divided into **three sections**: the **Citadel**, the **Middle Town**, and the **Lower Town**.
 
• The city was protected by massive **stone fortifications**, whereas most other Indus sites primarily used **mud-bricks** for defensive walls.
 
 
 
• **The Dholavira Signboard**:
 
 
• One of the most significant archaeological finds at the site is a large **inscription** consisting of **ten large-sized signs** of the **Harappan script**, often called the **Dholavira Signboard**.
 
• This discovery is unique because most **Indus Valley** scripts are found on small **seals** or **pottery** fragments rather than large public displays.
 
 
 
• **General Harappan Features**:
 
 
• While **complex drainage systems** and **large fortifications** are present in Dholavira, they are common traits across major sites like **Harappa**, **Mohenjo-daro**, and **Kalibangan**.
 
• **Pictorial murals** are not a standard architectural feature of the **Indus Valley Civilization**, which focused more on **terracotta figurines** and **steatite seals**.

questions.question: What is the primary goal of India’s Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act of 2003?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To control fiscal deficits**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act** was enacted in **August 2003** to institutionalize financial discipline and reduce the **fiscal deficit** of the Indian government.
 
• Its primary objective is to ensure **inter-generational equity** in fiscal management and long-term **macro-economic stability** by achieving a balanced budget over time.
 
• The Act originally mandated the **Central Government** to reduce the **fiscal deficit** to a target of **3% of the GDP** and to eliminate the **revenue deficit** entirely.
 
• It requires the government to lay three specific policy statements before **Parliament**: the **Medium-term Fiscal Policy Statement**, the **Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement**, and the **Macro-economic Framework Statement**.
 
• The act also aims to provide the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** with greater autonomy in managing **inflation** by prohibiting the government from borrowing directly from the RBI.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fiscal Deficit Components**:

 
 
• **Fiscal Deficit** is the difference between total expenditure and non-debt receipts, representing the total **borrowing needs** of the government.
 
• **Revenue Deficit** refers to the excess of **revenue expenditure** over **revenue receipts**, signifying that the government is borrowing to fund daily consumption.
 
 
 
• **N.K. Singh Committee (2016)**:
 
 
• This committee was formed to review the **FRBM Act** and recommended a **debt-to-GDP ratio** of **60%** (40% for the Centre and 20% for States) by the year **2023**.
 
• It introduced the **Escape Clause**, allowing the government to deviate from the **fiscal deficit** target by up to **0.5%** in cases of **national security**, structural reforms, or **major calamities**.

questions.question: The Preamble to the Constitution of India is primarily based on which resolution drafted and introduced by Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Objectives Resolution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Preamble** of the **Indian Constitution** is based on the **Objectives Resolution**, which was drafted and moved in the **Constituent Assembly** by **Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru** on **December 13, 1946**.
 
• The resolution outlined the fundamental commitments of the **Constituent Assembly** to create an independent, sovereign, and democratic **India**.
 
• It served as a guiding roadmap for the framing of the **Constitution**, emphasizing values such as **social, economic, and political justice**, **equality of status and opportunity**, and **freedom of thought, expression, belief, faith, and worship**.
 
• The **Constituent Assembly** officially and unanimously adopted the **Objectives Resolution** on **January 22, 1947**.
 
• The core philosophy and idealistic essence of this resolution were ultimately distilled into the **Preamble**, which serves as the **Identity Card** of the **Constitution**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Rights Resolution**:

 
 
• Historically associated with the **Karachi Session** of the **Indian National Congress** in **1931**, which was presided over by **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel** and emphasized civil liberties and economic programs.
 
 
 
• **Directive Principles Resolution**:
 
 
• The **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)** are contained in **Part IV** (Articles 36−51). These were borrowed from the **Irish Constitution** and aim to establish a **welfare state**.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Duties Resolution**:
 
 
• These were not part of the original document but were added to **Part IV-A** (Article 51A) by the **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976**, following the recommendations of the **Swaran Singh Committee**.
 
 
 
• The **Preamble** has been amended only once till date, in **1976**, to include the words **Socialist**, **Secular**, and **Integrity**.

questions.question: The Indian Council Act of ______ introduced the concept of 'separate electorate' in India.

• The **Indian Council Act of 1909** is popularly known as the **Morley-Minto Reforms**, named after the then Secretary of State for India, **Lord Morley**, and the Viceroy of India, **Lord Minto**.
 
• The most landmark and controversial provision of this Act was the introduction of **separate electorates** for Muslims, which allowed Muslim representatives to be elected only by Muslim voters.
 
• By granting **communal representation**, the Act effectively institutionalized the **divide and rule** policy, which later significantly influenced the socio-political fabric of India.
 
• Due to the introduction of this communal voting system, **Lord Minto** became known in historical texts as the **Father of Communal Electorate**.
 
• The Act increased the size of the **Legislative Councils** at both the Central and Provincial levels; for instance, the number of members in the **Central Legislative Council** was raised from 16 to 60.
 
• It also marked the first time an Indian was appointed to the **Viceroy’s Executive Council**, with **Satyendra Prasad Sinha** joining as a Law Member.

• Introduced the **Portfolio System**, where individual members of the executive council were placed in charge of specific departments.
 
• Started the process of **decentralization** by restoring legislative powers to the **Madras** and **Bombay** presidencies.
 
• Authorized the Viceroy to issue **ordinances** in times of emergency, which would have the force of law for six months.

questions.question: What is/are the element(s) or compound(s) that can be used in black and white photography?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**AgCl and AgBr**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Silver Bromide (AgBr)** and **Silver Chloride (AgCl)** are the primary light-sensitive chemicals used in **black and white photography**. They belong to a group of compounds known as **silver halides**.
 
• When these compounds are exposed to light, they undergo a **photochemical decomposition** reaction. In this process, the silver halide crystals absorb photons, causing the silver ions to be reduced to **metallic silver**.
 
• The chemical equation for the decomposition of **Silver Chloride** is: 2AgCl(s) + Sunlight → 2Ag(s) + Cl₂(g). The white silver chloride turns **greyish** due to the formation of silver metal.
 
• The chemical equation for **Silver Bromide** is: 2AgBr(s) + Sunlight → 2Ag(s) + Br₂(g). In this reaction, the pale yellow silver bromide decomposes into **metallic silver** and bromine gas.
 
• In the photographic process, the areas of the film exposed to more light contain more **silver metal**, which creates the dark parts of the negative, while unexposed areas remain clear after processing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Silver Halides**:

 
 
• These are compounds formed between **Silver (Ag)** and **Halogens** (Group 17 elements like Chlorine, Bromine, and Iodine).
 
• **AgBr** is the most widely used halide in photographic emulsions because it has the optimal level of sensitivity to light.
 
• **AgCl** is often used in **photographic printing paper** rather than the film itself, as it is less sensitive than bromide but produces finer detail.
 
 
 
• **Photodecomposition**:
 
 
• This is a type of **decomposition reaction** where a single reactant breaks down into two or more products in the presence of **photons** (light energy).
 
• This reaction is **endothermic** in nature as it requires the absorption of energy to break chemical bonds.
 
• Aside from photography, photolysis plays a critical role in **ozone layer formation** and **photosynthesis** in plants.

• It is geographically distinguished by its extensive **backwaters**, locally referred to as **Kayals**, which are a chain of brackish lagoons and lakes linked by man-made and natural canals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• It is notably famous for receiving heavy rainfall during the **North-East Monsoon** or **Retreating Monsoon** season.

• This is a geographical division of the **Eastern Coastal Plain** lying between the **Mahanadi** and **Krishna** rivers.
 
• It encompasses the coastal regions of **Odisha** and northern **Andhra Pradesh**, characterized by the **Chilika Lake**, the largest brackish water lagoon in India.
 
 
 
• **The Andhra Coast**
 
 
• Part of the **Eastern Coastal Plain**, it is known for its fertile **alluvial soil** and the presence of the **Kolleru Lake**, a major freshwater lake located between the Krishna and Godavari deltas.

questions.question: Which optical instrument is used to correct the eye defect known as Hypermetropia (or long-sightedness), where light focuses behind the retina?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Convex Lens**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hypermetropia**, commonly referred to as **long-sightedness**, is a refractive defect of the eye where light rays from nearby objects do not converge soon enough and instead focus at a point **behind the retina**.
 
• This condition occurs when the **axial length** of the eyeball is too short or the **crystalline lens** lacks sufficient curvature, resulting in a **focal length** that is too long for the eye's physical dimensions.
 
• A **Convex Lens** is a **converging lens** that is thicker at the center than at the edges. It works by bending incoming light rays inward before they reach the eye's natural lens.
 
• By adding a convex lens, the overall **optical power** of the eye is increased. This additional convergence ensures that the focal point is pulled forward and placed precisely on the **retina**, allowing for clear near vision.
 
• The power of the corrective lens required is measured in **Dioptres** (D) and is expressed as a positive value for **Hypermetropia**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concave Lens**:

 
 
• This is a **diverging lens** used to correct **Myopia** (short-sightedness).
 
• In a myopic eye, light focuses in **front of the retina** because the eyeball is too long or the lens is too curved; the concave lens spreads the rays out to shift the focus back onto the retina.
 
 
 
• **Cylindrical Lens**:
 
 
• These lenses have different powers in different meridians and are primarily used to correct **Astigmatism**.
 
• Astigmatism is caused by an irregular, non-spherical curvature of the **cornea** or lens, leading to distorted images.
 
 
 
• **Photochromic Lenses**:
 
 
• These are specialized lenses that darken when exposed to **Ultraviolet (UV) radiation** and clear up in the absence of UV light.
 
• They typically contain **silver halide** molecules and are used for light sensitivity and sun protection rather than specific refractive correction.

questions.question: The stabilisation measures introduced under India’s New Economic Policy (NEP) of 1991 were primarily aimed at achieving which of the following immediate objectives?

options.text: Correcting balance of payment imbalances and controlling inflationary pressures
Generating rural employment opportunities and strengthening agrarian livelihoods
Promoting disinvestment of public sector enterprises and reducing state control
Encouraging foreign direct investment inflows and improving capital availability

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Correcting balance of payment imbalances and controlling inflationary pressures**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **New Economic Policy (NEP)** launched in **July 1991** by the Indian government was a response to a severe economic crisis characterized by a massive **Balance of Payments (BoP)** deficit and skyrocketing **inflation**.
 
• The policy framework was broadly divided into two sets of measures: **Stabilisation Measures** and **Structural Reform Measures**.
 
• **Stabilisation Measures** were short-term in nature and were intended to correct the immediate weaknesses of the economy, specifically by restoring **macro-economic stability**.
 
• The first immediate objective was to improve the **foreign exchange reserves** to ensure India could meet its international payment obligations and avoid a sovereign default.
 
• The second objective was to control the **inflationary pressures** by regulating the money supply and fiscal deficit, as the inflation rate had reached double digits (approximately 17%) by **1991**.
 
• These measures were a prerequisite for receiving financial assistance from international agencies like the **International Monetary Fund (IMF)** and the **World Bank**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Structural Reform Measures**

 
 
• These were long-term policies aimed at improving the efficiency of the economy and increasing its international competitiveness.
 
• They included the famous **LPG** model: **Liberalisation**, **Privatisation**, and **Globalisation**.
 
• **Disinvestment**: This involves the government selling its equity in **Public Sector Enterprises (PSEs)** to private investors to reduce state control and improve corporate governance.
 
• **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)**: Policy changes were made to allow greater automatic approval for foreign capital to improve technological standards and capital availability.
 
• **Trade Policy Reforms**: These involved the removal of licensing for imports and the reduction of high **tariff rates** to integrate the Indian economy with the global market.

questions.question: Which of the following languages was conferred Classical Language status in October 2024?

• On **October 3, 2024**, the **Union Cabinet**, chaired by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, officially approved the conferment of **Classical Language** status to **Marathi** along with four other languages.

questions.question: As computer generations progressed, which of the following has been a trend that is generally true?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Computers became smaller and faster**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The transition from **Vacuum Tubes** in the first generation to **Transistors** in the second generation initiated a significant reduction in physical footprint and heat generation.
 
• The development of **Integrated Circuits (ICs)** during the third generation allowed for thousands of components to be placed on a single silicon chip, drastically increasing **processing speed** and reliability.
 
• Advancements in **Microprocessor** technology, specifically **Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI)**, enabled the compression of an entire **Central Processing Unit (CPU)** onto a single chip, leading to the **miniaturization** seen in modern laptops and smartphones.
 
• As the physical distance between electronic components decreased, the time required for electrical signals to travel was reduced, resulting in higher **clock speeds** and the ability to perform **billions of instructions per second (BIPS)**.
 
• Successive generations have consistently improved **energy efficiency** and **memory density**, allowing computers to store more data and operate faster while consuming less power than their predecessors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Computer Generations Breakdown**:

 
 
• **First Generation (1940-1956)**: Utilized **Vacuum Tubes**; these machines like **ENIAC** and **UNIVAC** were room-sized and frequently overheated.
 
• **Second Generation (1956-1963)**: Replaced tubes with **Transistors**, making computers smaller, faster, cheaper, and more energy-efficient.
 
• **Third Generation (1964-1971)**: Introduced **Integrated Circuits (ICs)**, which increased speed and efficiency by mounting many transistors on **Silicon Chips**.
 
• **Fourth Generation (1971-Present)**: Characterized by **Microprocessors** and **VLSI** technology; this era saw the birth of **Personal Computers (PCs)** like the **Altair 8800** and **Apple II**.
 
• **Fifth Generation (Present and Beyond)**: Focuses on **Artificial Intelligence (AI)**, **Ultra Large Scale Integration (ULSI)**, and **Parallel Processing** to achieve human-like computing capabilities.

questions.question: Which archaeological sites, besides Keeladi, have contributed to validating Sangam texts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Adichanallur, Korkai, Alangulam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Adichanallur**, located in the **Thoothukudi** district of **Tamil Nadu**, is an **Iron Age** burial site where carbon dating of paddy husks and urns has pushed the timeline of **Tamil** civilization back to at least **905 BCE**, aligning with the early roots of the **Sangam era**.
 
• **Korkai** served as the ancient capital and primary port of the **Early Pandyas**; it is extensively mentioned in **Sangam literature** like **Purananuru** and **Akananuru** for its flourishing **pearl fishery**, which has been validated by archaeological finds of pearl oysters and brick structures.
 
• **Alangulam**, situated near the **Vaigai river** mouth in **Ramanathapuram**, was an important coastal trading center where excavations revealed **Roman pottery** (Arretine and Rouletted ware), confirming the international maritime trade descriptions found in **Sangam texts**.
 
• Together with **Keeladi**, these sites provide material proof of high **literacy** (Tamil-Brahmi script), **urbanization**, and an advanced **agrarian society** that was previously known only through literary traditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indus Valley Civilization Sites**

 
 
• **Lothal**, **Dholavira**, and **Harappa** belong to the **Bronze Age** (c. 2500–1900 BCE) and are located in the northwestern parts of the Indian subcontinent, far preceding the **Sangam period**.
 
 
 
• **Medieval and Rock-cut Sites**
 
 
• **Ajanta** and **Ellora** are world-famous for their **monastic complexes** and **mural paintings** in Maharashtra, largely dating from the 2nd century BCE to the 10th century CE.
 
• **Hampi** was the 14th-century capital of the **Vijayanagara Empire** in Karnataka, representing a much later historical epoch than the classical **Sangam** age.
 
 
 
• **North-Western Sites**
 
 
• **Mohenjo-Daro** and **Kalibangan** are core **Harappan** sites characterized by planned drainage and citadels, unrelated to the specific regional **Tamil Sangam** context.

questions.question: What is the value of one tonne in SI units?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10³ kg**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **tonne** (also known as a **metric ton**) is a non-SI unit of mass that is officially accepted for use with the **International System of Units (SI)**.
 
• The standard **SI unit of mass** is the **kilogram (kg)**.
 
• One **tonne** is defined as exactly **1,000 kilograms**, which is represented in scientific notation as **10³ kg**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **SI Base Unit of Mass:**

 
 
• The **kilogram** is one of the seven base units of the **SI system**.
 
• In 2019, the definition of the kilogram was redefined to be based on the fundamental physical constant known as the **Planck constant (h)**, which has a fixed numerical value of 6.62607015 × 10−³⁴ kg m² s−¹.
 
 
 
• **Other Metric Mass Conversions:**
 
 
• **Gram (g):** One gram is 10−³ kg. Consequently, one tonne is equivalent to 1,000,000 grams (10⁶ g).
 
• **Quintal:** A metric unit of mass equal to 100 kg (or 10² kg). Therefore, one tonne contains exactly ten quintals.
 
• **Megagram (Mg):** This is the official SI multi-unit for one million grams, which is mathematically identical to one tonne (1 Mg = 10³ kg).
